r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')

 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(t)
with Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').open('w') as f:
 for i in range(len(r.pages)):
  f.write(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n'+Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').read_text())
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important problem with a practical approach: expanding minority-class supervision using existing unlabeled nodes avoids synthesizing node features and graph connections.

Evaluation spans five datasets, three GNN architectures, imbalance ratios up to 100, and naturally imbalanced settings, with five repetitions and reported standard errors. Several gains are substantial: on CiteSeer with GCN at ratio 10, F1 improves from the strongest listed baseline's 56.32 to 64.94.

The pseudo-label accuracy diagnostics, component ablations, and sensitivity experiments provide useful evidence beyond aggregate performance. The appendix documents dataset construction, optimization, hardware, and hyperparameter ranges. No material ethical concern is apparent from the public-benchmark experiments.
weaknesses: Novelty relative to the closest prior method is insufficiently established. The paper itself describes M3S as filtering pseudo-labels through agreement with clustering assignments, closely matching DPAM, but provides no explicit M3S comparison or precise explanation of the distinction. Table 11's DPAM-plus-confidence variant partially addresses this question, but does not establish the full method's advantage over a carefully matched implementation of this predecessor.

The experiments do not cleanly isolate increasing imbalance. Table 13 changes majority-class supervision from 20 to 50 or 100 labels while retaining one minority label, and switches the training split construction. Consequently, trends across these ratios conflate imbalance, annotation budget, and sampling protocol. Controlled experiments are needed to support the claimed relationship between imbalance severity and the method's advantage.

Some supporting results are internally inconsistent. In Table 8, the GCN result at ratio 5 reports 11,593.6 aligned and 2,308.4 discarded nodes, totaling 13,902 despite an unlabeled population of 13,632. These sets are defined as a partition. Claims of consistent superiority also overlook the GraphSAGE losses on Computers-Random and the GAT balanced-accuracy loss on Flickr. Corrected tables and appropriately qualified conclusions are necessary.

The geometric filtering definition needs clarification. Equation 5 measures distance to the assigned class center, whereas Section 4.3 treats this as the nearest class center. Assigning labels to entire clusters does not guarantee that equivalence for individual members. This affects the asserted ordering of distances and the interpretation of the GI index.

The ablations support a useful combination, but do not establish every component's necessity. In Table 11, DGIN sometimes reduces F1, and the complete method nearly ties geometric ranking alone on PubMed (77.38 versus 77.32). A fixed-weight ranking combination is also missing, leaving the specific benefit of RBO-based weighting unresolved.

Reproduction and computational assessment remain incomplete despite the documented search ranges. Algorithm 1 does not explicitly implement the per-class quota or removal of selected nodes from the unlabeled pool; model reinitialization between rounds and selected configurations are unspecified. No implementation link or end-to-end runtime comparison accompanies the 40–100 retraining rounds. Together with the missing closest-method comparison and inconsistent supporting results, these gaps outweigh the promising accuracy gains.
